result.message: Read all 12 supplied evidence files for kind=code on operator selu_ (subject 9ac565b2..., the round-2 best code stored in .best_kernel.py:1-175). The candidate is a single-file Triton implementation whose `run(A)` computes SELU in place (scale/alpha constants identical to torch.selu_), handles contiguous, masked-tail, non-contiguous (stride-recomputed offsets) and empty inputs, returns A (matching definition.json:11-21 outputs=['out'], mutates A, returns_alias_of out=A), uses no torch/torch.ops computation, no host synchronization, no environment mutation, and no test-specific shapes or values (block sizes derive only from numel and dtype). I found no P0 conversion or test-contract defect: the catalog oracle (oracle.py:71-76) is an independent torch.selu_ reference that does not import the candidate, inputs are built independently (oracle.py:9-68), correctness workloads cover empty/1/1025/7x9 with strided variants over fp16/bf16/fp32 (correctness.jsonl:1-24), timing workloads cover 1024..4096x4096 over the same three dtypes (timing.jsonl:1-12), and reported evaluation is 36/36 PASSED with max_abs_error 0.001953125. All findings below are P1 advisories about latent correctness hazards, portability, cache growth, and reporting; I did not assert device execution or timing validity from static inspection. The measured evidence reports best_geo_mean 0.8839579 (optimize_definition_output.json:5), i.e. performance PASSED is not a speedup greater than one: ledger round 2 shows 10 of 12 timing workloads slower than the reference (0.916, 1.090, 0.916, 1.248, 0.913, 0.898, 0.866, 0.710, 0.904, 0.881, 0.869, 0.572), and the one verified device win from round 3 (timing-7 83.3->63.5 us) is not in the submitted code because that round was reverted (.ledger.json:2397-2412).
